messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: realtime-alert: p99 latency breach on model-serving-prod (us-west) — p99 = 2.9s, SLO=1.0s, detected 1799005428

maria: paging oncall, this looks like a real-time regression spike across streaming endpoints. Anyone oncall?

oncall-sre: I'm oncall — looking now. Can you confirm whether this is for chat streaming only or also non-streaming generate endpoints?

akshay: seeing elevated p95 and p99 on streaming routes (stream-chat & stream-completion). Non-stream generates are slightly up but within p95 band.

eva: curious if KV cache hitrate dropped? dashboard shows a sudden drop at 18:02 UTC. placing link: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/latency?view=streaming (open to oncall/eng)

oncall-sre: thanks, looking at metrics. p95 jumped from 200ms -> 800ms, p99 spiked to ~3s. Error rates unchanged. tail latency distribution shows a long tail starting at 18:01:40.

sam: logs show repeated redis cache-miss bursts for kvcache-redis-prod-1 -> 200ms extra per token sometimes. Might be Redis cluster GC?

akshay: checking redis metrics -> network latency for redis had a transient spike and a few 5xx from redis client. Correlates with host rotate at 18:01 (k8s node drain?).

oncall-sre: do we have an in-flight streaming stall pattern? i.e., streaming requests hanging on token flush? traces show stall in token-generator step around kernel-infer call.

maria: customers? cs-rep, any reports?

cs-rep: just one ticket from a power-user: slow responses on long streaming conversations, intermittent. No major outage reported, but a few users hitting timeouts on client side after ~2.5s.

oncall-sre: initial mitigation options: (1) shift traffic away from streaming variant (v2-q) to fallback variant v1 stable; (2) temporarily increase streaming pool capacity for us-west; (3) enable emergency fallback to non-streaming generate as degraded but functional; (4) investigate redis/node drain. Thoughts?

akshay: safest quick move is traffic routing -> set policy to prefer v1 for streaming routes for 5 minutes. That avoids risky infra changes. I can push routing change.

eva: if we shift traffic, ensure we keep canary % so we don't cause quality regression for customers. maybe 90% -> v1, 10% -> v2-q for telemetry.

oncall-sre: ok akshay, do it now. post the command you run so we can audit.

akshay: running routing change now

akshay: ```
# rdwctl routing set --route stream-chat --policy priority --variants model:rw-chat-v1=90,model:rw-chat-v2-q=10 --duration 300
```

akshay: calling deploy API...

deploy-bot: rollout started by akshay — routing change for stream-chat scheduled. change id roll-1799005432-1

oncall-sre: monitoring metrics now.

(30s pause)

oncall-sre: p99 dropped to 1.1s and p95 back to ~240ms. Redis errors reduced. Looks like routing helped.

maria: nice. keep watch for 10 minutes then we can revert if stable or keep longer while we root cause.

sam: collecting traces for impacted requests for further analysis. I exported spans for 18:01:20-18:03:00.

akshay: created temporary incident note and linked runbook: https://internal.redwood/incident/1799005432 - action: routing rollback if regressions happen

oncall-sre: customer-impact assessment: limited. ~2.8% of streaming requests exceeded SLO during the spike window (approx 18:01:20 - 18:04:00). A handful of customers may have observed client timeouts. No broad outage.

eva: root cause hypothesis: k8s node drain + redis failover overlap caused a transient kvcache miss storm which amplified tail latency on streaming path; streaming variant v2-q is more sensitive due to batched kv lookups and longer tokenization steps.

maria: next steps: 1) ops: review recent node drain/timing and adjust drain-poststop config; 2) infra: check redis failover health and anti-affinity; 3) runtime/serve: investigate why v2-q is so sensitive to cache misses and add graceful degrade to fall back to local memcache if redis latency high; 4) cs: follow up with affected customers.

oncall-sre: I will run a post-incident checklist and assign owners. creating jira: RDW-INC-1799005432

sam: pointer for investigation: traces show token-generator waiting on kvcache.GET for many tokens sequentially. possible improvement: parallelize KV lookups and add local LRU to reduce remote roundtrips.

akshay: keeping routing at 90/10 for now. I'll schedule a controlled rollback later tonight if redis fixes confirmed.

cs-rep: I'll message the affected customers with an FYI — short note that we observed elevated latency and mitigated by routing change; we'll follow up with root cause once available.

maria: thanks all. if anything spikes again, escalate to P1 and ping infra and runtime leads.

oncall-sre: last check (18:08 UTC): metrics stable, p99 under 900ms. closing live mitigation phase. moving to postmortem planning.

incident-bot: Incident RDW-INC-1799005432 created and assigned to oncall-sre. Incident severity: SEV-3 (customer-impact, partial).

maria: assigning owners in the ticket now (akshay for routing/infra, sam for runtime traces, eva for redis/infra). I'll set a follow-up meeting at 10:00 UTC to review preliminary findings.

oncall-sre: noted.

(END)
